\[
g = e^{\mathcal{F}^{-1}\{H\, \mathcal{F}\{\ln(1 + f)\}\}} - 1,\quad H = (\gamma_H - \gamma_L)\left(1 - e^{-c D^2 / D_0^2}\right) + \gamma_L,\quad \gamma_L = 0.5,\ \gamma_H = 2,\ D_0 = 0.05
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(f, g\): The input and output values
- \(\gamma_L, \gamma_H\): The low and high frequency gains
- \(c\): The sharpness
- \(D, D_0\): The distance from the center of the spectrum and the cutoff in cycles per pixel

An image is lighting times reflectance. The logarithm turns the product into a sum, so a linear filter can treat the two parts apart. Lighting changes slowly and sits at low frequencies, where H is gamma_L. Reflectance holds the detail at high frequencies, where H is gamma_H. With gamma_L below 1 and gamma_H above 1, the filter flattens the lighting and raises the detail. The response and the steps follow Gonzalez and Woods. The filter uses ln(1 + f) so that black pixels have a logarithm, and returns exp(s) - 1. D is the distance from the center of the spectrum in cycles per pixel.
